Scope narrowed to Pass 2 / CWE-78 (Command/Argument Injection).

target.projectDescription: Google's SLO (Service Level Objective) generator: reads SLO and shared YAML configs (local file, GCS URL, or request-supplied string), resolves a metric backend class and exporter classes by name, computes SLO/error-budget reports, and exports them to monitoring stacks (Cloud Monitoring, Datadog, Dynatrace, Prometheus, Elasticsearch, BigQuery, Pub/Sub). Three entry surfaces: a click CLI (slo_generator/cli.py), a Functions Framework (Flask) HTTP/CloudEvent API (slo_generator/api/main.py), and a config migrator (slo_generator/migrations/migrator.py).

framework.notes: flask.md was loaded because Flask scored as a secondary candidate, but its route-handler model does not apply: the project never creates a Flask app or registers routes itself. Source/sink shapes are therefore derived from repository evidence per references/python.md and references/patterns.md (language reference path), with flask.md consulted only for its request-object source cues (request.get_json/get_data/data).

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: External data enters through five faces: (1) the Functions Framework API: the raw request body (request.get_data() in http mode), the decoded JSON body (request.get_json()), CloudEvent fields (request.data base64 payload, request["time"], request["id"]) become the SLO config string parsed by yaml.safe_load (api/main.py:54-61) or the exported SLO report (api/main.py:92-94); (2) configuration files: local YAML paths, GCS gs:// URLs, or string content, all funneled through utils.load_config/parse_config with ${VAR} environment-variable substitution inside values (utils.py:132), and yaml.load with the unsafe yaml.Loader in the migrator (migrator.py:229/264); (3) environment variables (CONFIG_PATH, EXPORTERS_PATH, GOOGLE_FUNCTION_* , DEBUG, MIN_VALID_EVENTS, ...); (4) CLI arguments through click-decorated commands; (5) remote service data (GCS blob content, backend API responses decoded with json.loads). Command execution: there is NOT a single subprocess/os.system/os.popen/exec*/spawn* call site in project source. The only code-execution-shaped boundary is name-based dynamic resolution: config-controlled class/method names flow into importlib.import_module + getattr (utils.py:337), getattr(instance, method) (report.py:204), getattr(sys.modules[__name__], f"..._{version}") (migrator.py:78/87/139) and getattr(self.client, method) (dynatrace.py:296), followed by invocation of the resolved object.

sanitizerObservations: yaml.safe_load (not yaml.load) is used on the request-derived SLO config string at api/main.py:94 and utils.py:145; the migrator however uses the unsafe yaml.Loader at migrator.py:229/264
no shlex.quote / pipes.quote / shell-escaping helper exists anywhere in project source (no shell command construction at all)

class name selection (utils.py:301-323 import_cls) performs no allowlist check on the module path: any '.'-containing class name in config is imported verbatim as a plugin; core names are reassembled into a slo_generator.<type>s.<filename> path - snake_to_caml/capitalize normalization is cosmetic, not a security filter
no argv-list subprocess invocation exists, so no list-form command sanitization pattern applies

load_config falls back to parsing the path string itself as YAML content when the path does not exist (utils.py:88-89), blurring file/string input, but this is an input-shape property, not a sanitizer
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: Zero direct command-execution sinks exist in this snapshot; the subprocess/os.exec API families are kept in sinks.ql only as the exhaustive CWE-78 baseline. The dynamic import / getattr dispatch chain is a documented plugin extension point (docs/providers/custom.md, samples/custom/custom_backend.py), and normal name-based dispatch is not automatically a vulnerability: these are recorded as sink candidates for labeling, not findings. No CVE ground truth was consulted (see constraintsHonored).

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) and codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF (deferred to Phase 2)
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id/@tags only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
file (absolute path via Location API; AstNode.getFile() does not exist)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware, only genuine resolved calls into external modules (json/yaml/base64 decode APIs, importlib.import_module)
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, receiver name, assignment-to-call bindings); catches framework request objects (request.get_data/get_json/data/subscripts), os.environ shapes, getattr dispatch, Path/file reads, and config dict reads that API graphs cannot resolve. Subject to name-collision noise; the LLM labeling step filters it.

exclusions: tests/ (tests/unit/** including fixtures) excluded from candidate scope per the Augur candidate strategy (noise: test config loading and stub classes); implemented as a path filter in both queries
samples/custom/ kept in scope: it is the documented plugin-target shape for the dynamic import boundary, not test noise
logging-only helpers (LOGGER.debug/info calls, click.secho output) are not extracted as candidates; pure output sites are out of scope
migrations/ here means SLO-config format migration (v1->v2 migrator), not DB schema migrations; it stays in scope and is NOT subject to the migration-file FP heuristic

uncoveredCases: compute.py:119 'instance().export(data, **config)' - the callee is an Attribute of a Call result, so the dispatch_invocation family (Name callee assigned from a dispatch call in the same function) does not match it; mitigated by the export param rows of %Exporter classes and by the get_exporter_cls wrapper rows.

Functions Framework dispatch itself is outside the database: run_compute/run_export are registered by target name through the GOOGLE_FUNCTION_TARGET environment variable (cli.py:139); only the param family captures the request entry points.

api/main.py:54 'request.get_data().decode(\'utf-8\')' - only the get_data/get_json/data/subscript request shapes observed in this codebase are matched; other flask request fields (request.headers/args/form) do not occur in project source.
utils.py:118 'yaml.util.load_yaml_guess_indent(...)' - not expected to resolve through API graphs (accessed as an attribute chain on the yaml module object); matched at AST level only.

utils.py:132 'ctx[var]' env substitution happens inside the nested function replace_env_vars of parse_config; captured as an env-read row (ctx subscript), but the re.sub/str.replace interpolation into config content is not modeled as a flow step at extraction time.

Dynamic alias imports: none observed for the APIs of interest (importlib, yaml, json, base64, os imported directly); internal helpers are called by bare or module-attribute name, including the 'from slo_generator.compute import compute as _compute' alias at cli.py:28 which the internal_transfer family matches by the alias name '_compute'. If a backend module were loaded under an alias, the AST family still matches by attribute name.
CloudEvent fields other than data/time/id (e.g. source, type) are not read in project source; no coverage claimed.

google.cloud.storage, functions_framework, prometheus_http_client, googleapiclient are external dependencies not present in the database; their internals are out of scope (only call sites into them are extracted).
